messages.content: What kind of fertilizer is best for growing tomatoes?

function.name: soil_analysis_analyze_soil_type
function.description: Analyze a type of soil and provides characteristics about it. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

soil_type.description: The type of the soil. For example, loam, sandy, etc.

parameters_needed.description: Optional specific characteristics of the soil to analyze.

message.content: For tomatoes, a balanced fertilizer with a slightly higher middle number (nitrogen) is usually best. A common recommendation is a 5-10-5 or 10-10-10 NPK ratio, but many growers prefer a slightly higher potassium (K) to promote fruit set—something like 10-10-20. Look for a product labeled “tomato” or “fruiting” as it’s formulated for this purpose. If you’re using organic options, compost, well‑aged manure, or fish emulsion work well. Always follow the label instructions and consider doing a soil test first to tailor the exact mix to your garden’s needs.
